A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIQUE research work. All 22 pages of v3 and 29 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original simulations, analyses of concrete, lichen, and digit data, and appendix case studies and computational timing results.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds correlated-regression simulations, XGBoost lichen results, and several sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Equation 1 and Algorithm 1 retain the same quantile replacements and observation-specific cross-validated loss differences. Additional model applications, loss comparisons, and implementation explanations do not establish a change to CLIQUE's procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds a controlled regression scenario with 101 features, correlated Gaussian predictors, and context-dependent signal blocks (Section 3.4), including correlation-strength and marginal-effect variants in Appendix C. This substantially extends the independent, low-dimensional simulations in v3. The concrete, lichen, and digit datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain LIME, SHAP, and ICI. Local Permute already appears in v3's parameter analysis. Naming DeepSHAP clarifies the existing ANN comparison; XGBoost is an additional model being explained, rather than an importance-method baseline.

E3.justification: V4 introduces three-fold ANN evaluation for the correlated simulation, XGBoost evaluation on lichen, and controlled variations of CV folds, LIME kernel widths and bins, and loss functions. These substantially expand evaluation designs. The existing toy-simulation sample sizes, M = 25 setting, and zero-importance error criterion are retained.

E4.justification: V3's AND-gate replacement-count study is retained and extended to regression. V4 adds CV-fold stability analysis (Section 3.6), LIME tuning (Appendix A), absolute-versus-squared loss comparisons (Appendix B), and correlation and marginal-effect checks (Appendix C), addressing several previously untested robustness questions.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point estimates without reported run counts or uncertainty to estimates from 50 Monte Carlo simulations with 95% confidence intervals. This establishes new statistical reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v3. The timing results already reported 20-simulation summaries in both versions.

E6.justification: All four matched Table 1 rows have updated estimates; Regression is renamed Corners-Regression. CLIQUE's AND Gate entry changes from 0.005 to a 50-simulation estimate of 0.009 ± 0.001, while remaining lowest. New correlated-regression, XGBoost, and sensitivity findings substantially expand the results; these do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: CLIQUE's formal definition, properties P1–P8, Proposition 1 and its proof, and the complexity discussion are unchanged. The additional response equations specify new simulation designs rather than extending the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: V4 narrows the abstract, introduction, and conclusion's criticism of existing methods, emphasizing complementary loss-based information and criterion-specific advantages. The central contributions—model-agnostic local importance, interaction detection, quantile stability, and multiclass applicability—remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5.1 discusses out-of-distribution replacements, correlated predictors, model calibration and misspecification, and CV partition risks. V4 acknowledges that tuned LIME can recover interactions and explicitly restricts Table 1's interpretation to P1, replacing v3's broader false-positive interpretation.

D1.justification: V4 replaces a promised future code link with a repository address for R/Python functions and data/figure-generation code. It newly documents random five-fold CV, DeepSHAP use, LIME's 10 bins, and timing details including training costs and five-core parallelization. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: V4 adds Shrikumar et al. (2017) and Chen et al. (2020), expands SHAP and LIME descriptions, and more consistently emphasizes complementarity with prediction-based explanations. The principal related-work coverage and methodological lineage remain.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction, baseline explanations, simulation interpretations, and conclusion. The parameter study moves from Section 3.1.1 to 3.6, the conclusion gains separate limitations and discussion subsections, and the appendices are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V4 adds figures for correlated data, parameter sensitivity, XGBoost, LIME tuning, and loss comparisons, and expands Table 1's display with confidence intervals. Existing graphics are retained and relocated, including v3's Random Forest lichen Figures 9–10 becoming Figures 23–24 in Appendix D.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens the empirical support through repeated-simulation confidence intervals, controlled correlated-data experiments, and sensitivity analyses. Its explicit limitations and acknowledgment of tuned LIME address weaknesses in v3's broad comparative interpretations. More concrete implementation and code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains materially improve the paper while preserving its method and earlier evidence.
